subject.title: Feature: config option to route gateway lifecycle warnings to a dedicated channel

question: Should OpenClaw add a general internal-warning destination/category router under `messages`, and what categories/defaults should it support relative to existing suppression and cron failure destinations?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the implementation changes public config and warning-delivery semantics across gateway, agent, cron, and channel surfaces, so automation cannot safely choose the product contract.

options.title: Approve Default-Compatible Router
options.body: Add an explicit opt-in router for lifecycle, tool-error, and system-notice warnings while preserving current active-channel behavior by default.

options.title: Keep Suppression-Only Policy
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` and `cron.failureDestination` as the supported operator controls and narrow this issue to docs or specific leaks.

options.title: Split By Warning Class
options.body: Handle lifecycle warnings, tool errors, and cron notifications as separate narrowly owned issues instead of introducing one general router now.

recommendation.title: Approve Default-Compatible Router
recommendation.body: Add an explicit opt-in router for lifecycle, tool-error, and system-notice warnings while preserving current active-channel behavior by default.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on adjacent warning-delivery behavior and the superseded/canonical shared dispatch fixes.
